generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The introduction of `DEFAULT_ALLOW_PARTIAL_SEARCH_RESULTS` and `DEFAULT_ALLOW_PARTIAL_SEQUENCE_RESULTS` settings in the EqlPlugin class allows cluster administrators to control partial search behavior dynamically. This is a valuable feature for managing search operations in environments with potential shard failures.

The test configuration in EqlTestUtils now includes values for allowPartialSearchResults and allowPartialSequenceResults. This is important to ensure that tests cover scenarios with partial results enabled or disabled.

The changes to LocalStateEQLXPackPlugin make it implement CircuitBreakerPlugin and delegate circuit breaker methods to the EqlPlugin instance. This is a good approach to integrate circuit breaker functionality into the plugin.

The changes to the `Results` class constructor and `fromPayload` method correctly include shard failures in the results object. This ensures that shard failure information is preserved throughout the processing pipeline.

Adding random boolean values for allowPartialSearchResults and allowPartialSequenceResults in various test cases increases the diversity of scenarios covered by tests. This is beneficial for ensuring robustness.

These additions ensure that the request's allowPartialSearchResults and allowPartialSequenceResults settings are used if provided; otherwise, the cluster defaults are applied. This logic is correct and aligns with the intended behavior.

Both additions of `ShardSearchFailure.EMPTY_ARRAY` are correct as they initialize the shard failures array to empty when no shard failures have occurred yet. This ensures that the response object does not contain null values in this field.

review_comment: It would be great if all the existent tests in EQL that have no idea about partial results (all the tests based on BaseEqlSpecTestCase before this PR) would completely randomize these two new settings. All of them should behave completely the same because we have no "broken" shard setup for them which means that irrespective of the values provided, the tests should pass.
There is some randomization already, but I'm making it more complete.

review_comment:
`allowPartialResultsInBody` value seems to suggest that "partial results" settings can be used **either** as request parameter or request body parameter. I think we should test the case when the user provides:
- request parameter values AND request body parameters (both of them or just one)
- either one of them

In other words, randomize any combination of request parameters presence and values in the two places where we allow them.
What happens if an user provides only `allow_partial_sequece_results=true` or uses `allow_partial_search_results=false` and `allow_partial_sequece_results=true` at the same time?

`allow_partial_sequece_results` alone (or with  `allow_partial_search_results=false`) has no effect.
There are randomized tests for this in [PartialSearchResultsIT](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/116388/files#diff-394483381f9a9290704dec509e32ba564499cf341a3b0ee536f7463537137aebR210) , but probably I can extend them a bit, randomly setting `allow_partial_search_results=false`
